title: Authorship and the Politics and Ethics of LLM Watermarks

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical evaluation of how entropy differences across different natural languages (e.g., high-resource vs. low-resource languages), translation tasks, and linguistic registers (e.g., native vs. non-native speakers) affect the detectability and false-negative rates of LLM watermarks.

Conceptual analysis of how text generation constrained by specific topics or educational levels (e.g., highly standardized texts intended for lower education levels or specific migrant demographics) exhibits lower entropy, leading to disparate impacts in watermarking vulnerability.
